title: You're Probably Overpaying for AI by 10x
description:
Paying the same rate for an AI that sorts an email as one that solves a complex reasoning problem is the equivalent of flying a private jet to pick up groceries. Both accomplish the task, and only one of them makes financial sense at that price point.

The rule that fixes this is simple. Match the size of the AI to the size of the job.

High-capacity models earn their cost on genuine complexity. Real reasoning, messy multi-step problems, judgment calls where getting the nuance wrong has real consequences. Those tasks justify the price.
Sorting an email into a category, tagging a lead, answering a predictable support question from a knowledge base. Those do not. A smaller, faster model handles all three with equal accuracy and spends a fraction of the tokens doing it.

The savings compound across every routine step inside a live automation running daily volume over a month. That is not a marginal difference.
